newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-NIEKRO ELECTED TO HALL OF FAME; SUTTON FALLS SHORT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NIEKRO ELECTED TO HALL OF FAME; SUTTON FALLS SHORT.

text.p: Phil Niekro, a 300-game winner whose knuckleball baffled major league hitters for 24 seasons, Monday was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame.
Niekro received votes on 380 of 473 ballots cast by the Baseball Writers Association of America, surpassing the 75 percent (355 votes) needed for election into the Hall.

Don Sutton, the only other eligible 300-game winner not yet in the Hall of Fame, fell nine votes short of baseball's ultimate honour. The long-time Dodgers pitcher was named on 73.15 percent of the ballots, collecting 346 votes.
Induction ceremonies will take place this summer at the Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, New York.
Niekro played for bad ballclubs for most of his career, but managed to compile 318 wins in 24 years with the Milwaukee/Atlanta Braves, New York Yankees and Cleveland Indians before retiring in 1987.
Behind his trademark knuckleball, Niekro posted a 318-274 record with a 3.35 lifetime Earned Run Average and 3,342 strikeouts in 5,404 innings.

Niekro, who never pitched in a World Series, was a five-time All-Star and five-time Gold Glove winner. He holds the National League record for putouts by a pitcher (340) and shares the major-league mark for most years with 200 or more innings pitched (19) with Hall of Famer Cy Young.
Sutton was 324-256 with a 3.26 ERA in 23 seasons, generally playing on better teams than did Niekro.
Niekro will become the 18th 300-game winner enshrined in Cooperstown with Nolan Ryan a lock for election when he becomes eligible in 1999.
Niekro had been on the Hall of Fame ballot for five years. Last year when no players were voted in for the first time since 1971, Niekro fell 32 votes shy (68.30 percent).
The only other player named on more than half the ballots was first baseman Tony Perez with 312 votes (65.96 percent).
Niekro becomes the 229th member of the Hall, which is comprised of 174 former players, 22 pioneers-executives, 13 Negro Leaguers, 13 managers and seven umpires.

Additional inductees for Cooperstown could be named by the Veterans Committee, the group that votes on overlooked players and managers, umpires and former Negro League stars. The Veterans Committee will meet March 5 in Tampa.
